newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian miners' union votes to end strike - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russian miners' union votes to end strike - agency.

text.p: The leadership of Russia's Rosugleprof coal miners' union decided at a meeting late on Wednesday to end a nationwide strike it launched on December 3, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass said the union leaders decided to resume work at pits and open cast mines on Thursday after the government had agreed to meet some of the miners' demand, including a promise to pay back wage arrears before the end of the year. Neither the union nor the government were available for comment.

Up to 400,000 miners in nearly 200 pits and open cast mines across Russia have taken part in the protest. The union says goverment debt to the industry is worth around two trillion roubles ($400 million) and even greater company debt had led to huge delays in paying out wages.

At some mines the workers also demanded the resignation of the government and a dramatic change of the current course of economic reform. But the majority of strikers stopped short of making political demands.

Pro-democracy strikes by coal miners in 1989 and 1990 helped Russian President Boris Yeltsin in his struggle against the communist administration which ended with the collapse of the Soviet Union in late 1991.
But bold market reforms launched by Yeltsin after the victory turned out to be damaging for the mines, most of which are loss-making.
